dry: Drivers in {state} complain of unofficial fees at checkpoints.
Unofficial checkpoint fees anger drivers across {state}.
wahala: Drivers in {state} say checkpoints now collect fees faster than tollgates.
Checkpoint 'welcome fees' have become a way of life in {state}.

dry: An audit of checkpoints in {state} leads to suspensions.
Officers in {state} are suspended after a checkpoint audit.
wahala: Audit team visits checkpoints in {state}; the fees reportedly took the day off.
Officers in {state} suspended after audit, the receipts still missing.

dry: The presidency condemns illegal checkpoint fees in {state}.
A stern statement on checkpoint fees is issued.
wahala: Presidency warns checkpoints in {state}; checkpoints reply with a new price list.
Stern statement issued, the fees unmoved.

dry: A vigilante group in {state} refuses to hand over patrols to the police.
{governor} asks Abuja for guidance on a vigilante group in {state}.
wahala: Vigilantes in {state} say they will hand over patrols when the roads are safe, which is not today.
{governor} asks Abuja what to do about vigilantes everyone depends on.

dry: Officers seize a large weapons cache near the border of {state}.
A weapons shipment is intercepted at the {state} border.
wahala: Officers seize a weapons cache in {state}; the paperwork alone took longer than the chase.
A weapons shipment is stopped at the {state} border, and a press conference follows.

dry: Communal clashes in {state} leave several dead and a curfew is requested.
{governor} asks for federal support after clashes in {state}.
wahala: Communal clashes in {state} leave several dead. A curfew has been requested.
{governor} asks Abuja for support after clashes in {state}.

dry: A curfew and troop deployment begin in {state}.
Troops arrive in {state} as a curfew takes effect.
wahala: A curfew and troops are in place in {state}.
Troops deploy to {state}; a curfew is in force.

dry: A mediation panel begins talks between the communities in {state}.
Community leaders meet a federal panel in {state}.
wahala: A mediation panel begins talks in {state}.
Community leaders meet a federal panel in {state}.

dry: The federal government leaves the clashes in {state} to the state.
No federal response yet to the clashes in {state}.
wahala: The federal government leaves the clashes in {state} to the state.
No federal response yet to the clashes in {state}.

dry: Families displaced by violence are sheltering in schools in {state}.
Displaced families in {state} need food, water and shelter.
wahala: Families displaced by violence are sheltering in schools in {state}.
Displaced families in {state} need food, water and shelter.

dry: Long queues form at ATMs as cash runs short nationwide.
Cash scarcity hits banks across the country.
wahala: Queues at ATMs now have their own food vendors as cash runs short.
Cash scarcity hits banks nationwide; transfers have become the new currency.

dry: Oil prices surge, lifting expected government revenue.
A jump in crude prices boosts the oil income forecast.
wahala: Oil price jumps and everybody suddenly has a spending plan.
Crude prices surge, and the Treasury is already getting letters.

dry: Oil prices slump, cutting projected revenue.
A fall in crude prices opens a hole in the oil income forecast.
wahala: Oil price slumps and the budget now needs a miracle.
Crude prices fall; the revenue forecast says 'abeg'.

dry: Container backlogs grow at the {state} port.
Importers face weeks of delay at the {state} port.
wahala: Containers pile up at the {state} port, and so do the stamps.
Importers wait weeks at the {state} port while forms travel between offices.

dry: Traders in {state} close their stalls over a new levy.
Market closures in {state} follow a dispute over a levy.
wahala: Traders in {state} lock their stalls over a new levy and the whole market has gone quiet.
Market closes in {state} as traders say the levy has no receipt.

dry: A delegation of foreign investors tours the country.
Investors visit to assess business conditions.
wahala: A delegation of investors tours the country, shown the roads that were fixed last week.
Investors visit and are told everything is under control.

dry: A rating agency cuts the country's outlook, citing debt.
The country's credit outlook is downgraded.
wahala: A rating agency downgrades the country, and lenders send a longer invoice.
Credit outlook cut; the Treasury says the agency 'misunderstood' the debt.

dry: Farmers in {state} report a record harvest.
A bumper harvest in {state} floods local markets.
wahala: Farmers in {state} report a record harvest, and the tomatoes have started to negotiate.
A bumper harvest in {state} floods the market and prices dive.

dry: Measles cases rise among children in {state}.
Clinics in {state} report a rise in measles cases.
wahala: Measles cases rise among children in {state}.
Clinics in {state} report a rise in measles cases.

dry: More doctors leave the country for jobs abroad, hospitals report.
Hospitals warn of a growing shortage of doctors.
wahala: Doctors keep leaving for abroad and the wards are running on prayers and rotas.
Hospitals warn of a doctor shortage while visa offices report record queues.

dry: Inspectors seize counterfeit medicines in a {state} warehouse.
A raid in {state} uncovers a large stock of fake drugs.
wahala: Inspectors seize fake drugs in {state}; the label was perfect, the medicine was not.
A raid in {state} finds a warehouse of counterfeit drugs, receipts included.

dry: The main maternity ward in {state} closes for lack of staff and supplies.
A maternity ward in {state} shuts, sending patients to other clinics.
wahala: The main maternity ward in {state} closes for lack of staff and supplies.
A maternity ward in {state} shuts, sending patients to other clinics.

dry: A heatwave warning is issued for {state} as temperatures climb.
{state} braces for several days of dangerous heat.
wahala: A heatwave warning is issued for {state} as temperatures climb.
{state} braces for several days of dangerous heat.

dry: A growing gully threatens homes and a road in {state}.
Gully erosion forces families to leave homes in {state}.
wahala: A gully in {state} is eating a road, and the committee is eating the budget.
Gully erosion threatens homes in {state}, and a site visit is scheduled.

dry: Dry-season fires spread across farmland in {state}.
Fires threaten villages and farms in {state}.
wahala: Dry-season fires spread across farmland in {state}.
Fires threaten villages and farms in {state}.

dry: A bridge collapses in {state}, cutting a main route.
Rescue teams respond to a bridge collapse in {state}.
wahala: A bridge collapses in {state}, cutting a main route.
Rescue teams respond to a bridge collapse in {state}.

dry: Rescue work ends and a rebuild begins in {state}.
Federal funds approved to rebuild the bridge in {state}.
wahala: Rescue work ends and a rebuild begins in {state}.
Federal funds approved to rebuild the bridge in {state}.

dry: A temporary crossing opens near the collapsed bridge in {state}.
Traffic resumes on a temporary crossing in {state}.
wahala: A temporary crossing opens near the collapsed bridge in {state}.
Traffic resumes on a temporary crossing in {state}.

dry: An inquiry is ordered into the bridge collapse in {state}.
A panel will investigate the bridge collapse in {state}.
wahala: An inquiry is ordered into the bridge collapse in {state}; the committee has been named.
A panel will investigate the bridge collapse in {state}, report due eventually.

dry: Gas supply to several power plants is cut over unpaid bills.
A gas supply dispute reduces power generation nationwide.
wahala: Gas supplier cuts plants over unpaid bills, and light is now on a payment plan.
A gas dispute reduces power generation, and generators get busy.

dry: Vandals strip a transmission tower in {state}, cutting power to several towns.
Power is cut across parts of {state} after tower vandalism.
wahala: Thieves strip a transmission tower in {state}, and the towns went dark by dinner.
Power is cut across parts of {state} after someone stole a piece of the grid.

dry: A developer offers solar mini-grids for communities in {state}.
Solar mini-grid plans are proposed for {state}.
wahala: A developer offers solar mini-grids for {state}, panels included, delays negotiable.
Solar mini-grid plans proposed for {state}; the meeting about the meeting is set.

dry: Lawmakers are accused of adding unrequested projects to the budget.
A row over budget padding erupts in the Assembly.
wahala: Lawmakers accused of padding the budget, with a few roads that exist only on paper.
A budget padding row erupts and every project is somebody's cousin's.

dry: A payroll check in {state} finds hundreds of workers who do not exist.
Ghost workers are found on the {state} payroll.
wahala: A payroll check in {state} finds workers who have never been seen, yet never miss payday.
Ghost workers found on the {state} payroll, and they are very punctual.

dry: Party primaries end in competing congresses and court orders.
Chaos hits party primaries across several states.
wahala: Party primaries turn into competing congresses, court orders and rented chairs.
Chaos at primaries, with three winners declared in one hall.

dry: A whistleblower leaks documents on inflated ministry contracts.
Leaked documents show contracts awarded far above market value.
wahala: A whistleblower leaks documents on contracts priced like gold-plated roundabouts.
Leaked documents show ministry contracts at several times their value.

dry: University lecturers begin a nationwide strike over pay and funding.
Campuses close as lecturers go on strike.
wahala: University lecturers begin a nationwide strike and students start a lot of side businesses.
Campuses close as lecturers strike over pay and funding.

dry: The government meets the lecturers' main demands and the strike ends.
Lecturers suspend their strike after a funding deal.
wahala: The government meets the lecturers' main demands and the strike ends.
Lecturers suspend their strike after a funding deal.

dry: The government makes a partial offer to striking lecturers.
Talks continue after a partial offer to lecturers.
wahala: The government makes a partial offer to striking lecturers.
Talks continue after a partial offer to lecturers.

dry: The strike enters a second month with no deal in sight.
Students remain at home as the lecturers' strike drags on.
wahala: The strike enters a second month and graduation is now a rumour.
Students stay home as the lecturers' strike drags on.

dry: Students march in several cities over closed campuses.
Student groups protest the lecturers' strike.
wahala: Students march in several cities over closed campuses and shut a few roundabouts.
Student groups protest the strike, and the placards are well spelt.

dry: Thousands of young people march to demand jobs.
A march over youth unemployment draws large crowds.
wahala: Thousands of young people march for jobs, with a CV on every placard.
A march over youth unemployment draws large crowds in several cities.

dry: Rival claims to a traditional throne divide {state}.
A dispute over a traditional ruler lands in court in {state}.
wahala: Rival claims to a traditional throne divide {state}, and both claimants have printed invitations.
A dispute over a traditional ruler lands in court in {state}.

dry: The national football team wins a major match, and the country celebrates.
Celebrations erupt after the national team's victory.
wahala: The national team wins and the whole country forgets the fuel queue for one night.
Celebrations erupt after the national team's victory, and every generator is on.

dry: The road transport union parks vehicles in a nationwide strike.
Travellers are stranded as transport workers strike over levies and roads.
wahala: Transport workers park their vehicles and the roads suddenly feel very empty.
Travellers are stranded as transport workers strike over levies and roads.

dry: Gridlock freezes {state} for a full working day.
A traffic standstill costs {state} a day of work.
wahala: Gridlock freezes {state}; some commuters report they have started to pay rent in the traffic.
A traffic standstill costs {state} a full day of work.

dry: Blocked drains overflow in {state}, flooding streets and homes.
Emergency teams respond to flooding across {state}.
wahala: Blocked drains overflow in {state}, flooding streets and homes.
Emergency teams respond to flooding across {state}.

dry: Manufacturers propose restarting idle textile mills in {state}.
A textile revival plan is presented for {state}.
wahala: Manufacturers propose restarting the idle textile mills in {state}, if the lights stay on.
A textile revival plan is presented for {state}, complete with real numbers.

dry: Taps run dry in several districts of {state}.
Water shortages hit parts of {state}.
wahala: Taps run dry in several districts of {state}, and water sellers set the new rate.
Water shortages hit parts of {state}, and buckets are the new status symbol.

dry: A pipeline leak fouls creeks and fishing grounds in {state}.
Residents report a spill that has run for days in {state}.
wahala: A pipeline leak fouls creeks and fishing grounds in {state}.
Residents report a spill that has run for days in {state}.

dry: A cleanup is ordered after the oil spill in {state}.
The operator is told to clean up the spill in {state}.
wahala: A cleanup is ordered after the oil spill in {state}.
The operator is told to clean up the spill in {state}.

dry: Compensation is announced for fishing communities in {state}.
Affected families in {state} will receive compensation.
wahala: Compensation is announced for fishing communities in {state}.
Affected families in {state} will receive compensation.

dry: The operator says it is investigating the spill in {state}.
No cleanup yet in {state} as the investigation continues.
wahala: The operator says it is investigating the spill in {state}; residents say they have been investigating it for days.
No cleanup yet in {state} as the investigation continues.

dry: Fishing communities block a jetty in {state} over the spill.
A protest at a jetty in {state} disrupts operations.
wahala: Fishing communities block a jetty in {state} over the spill.
A protest at a jetty in {state} disrupts operations.

dry: Dock workers strike at the main port in {state} over delayed pay.
Ships queue at the {state} port as workers strike.
wahala: Dock workers strike over delayed pay and the ships are waiting with their meters running.
Ships queue at the {state} port as workers strike.

dry: Thousands of families are resettled in communities in {state}.
Resettlement begins for families returning to {state}.
wahala: Thousands of families are resettled in communities in {state}.
Resettlement begins for families returning to {state}.

dry: Farmers in {state} ask to return to land that has been unsafe for years.
A plan to reopen farmland is proposed in {state}.
wahala: Farmers in {state} ask to return to land that has been unsafe for years.
A plan to reopen farmland is proposed in {state}.

dry: Federal civil servants march in {state} over delayed allowances.
Workers protest outside ministries in {state}.
wahala: Federal civil servants march in {state} over delayed allowances; the ministries closed early to join them.
Workers protest outside ministries in {state}.

dry: Demolitions begin at estates with disputed land papers in {state}.
Residents protest demolitions in {state}.
wahala: Bulldozers arrive at estates in {state}, and the approvals are somewhere in the rubble.
Residents protest demolitions in {state}.
